name: 3D Cursor Flythrough
description: A glossy 3D pointer swoops in from close to the camera, banks into its turns, hovers a nav tab, clicks Upgrade (the button turns green), hovers a chart point for a tooltip, then flies off — with real motion blur and a height-aware shadow.
move: A glossy 3D pointer swoops in from close to the camera, banks into its turns, hovers a nav tab, clicks Upgrade (the button turns green), hovers a chart point for a tooltip, then flies off — with real motion blur and a height-aware shadow.
how: three.js perspective camera matched to stage pixels at z=0, so the pointer tip projects exactly onto DOM targets measured after fonts load. The pointer is a rounded, beveled extrusion with clearcoat over a generated studio environment. Legs are eased arcs that rise off the page; banking and lean come from velocity. Fast frames average up to 10 sub-frame renders (motion blur). A DOM shadow grows and softens with height.
adapt: Re-target LEGS to your UI's elements; --cursor and --cursor-rim colour the pointer. Placeholder copy is generic. Colours come from the palette tokens at the top of the page (--bg, --surface, --ink, --muted, --accent, --accent-2); change those to re-brand it.
port: Pure draw(t): mount the markup in the shot and call draw from the film's frame hook with shot-local time; wait for fonts before measuring.
caveats: Original implementation of the "3D cursor" motion-design idea; no third-party preset, kit or brand assets.
Starts and ends on its opening frame so it loops; trim the exit when cutting to the next shot.
